requirements.statement: Open with a Summary section: one paragraph on who, what, where, and the decision.
Then a Facts section. Every fact cites the document in the file it comes from, in square brackets: [notice of loss], [police report], [invoice 1].

source: (text, request, material) => { const names = material.map(m => m.name.toLowerCase().replace(/\.[^.]*$/, '').replace(/[-_]/g, ' ').trim()); const factSec = text.split(/^## /m).find(s => /^Facts/i.test(s)); if (!factSec) return { ok: true, detail: 'no Facts section', spans: [] }; const body = factSec.replace(/^Facts[^\n]*\n/, ''); const sentences = body.split(/(?<=[.!?])\s+/).filter(s => s.trim()); const bad = []; let pos = text.indexOf(body); for (const s of sentences) { const idx = text.indexOf(s, pos); const cites = [...s.matchAll(/\[([^\]]+)\]/g)].map(m => m[1].toLowerCase().trim()); if (!/\d|[A-Za-z]/.test(s)) continue; if (cites.length === 0) { bad.push({ start: idx, end: idx + s.length, why: 'fact without a document citation' }); } else if (cites.some(c => !names.some(n => n === c || n.includes(c) || c.includes(n)))) { bad.push({ start: idx, end: idx + s.length, why: 'citation not a document in the file' }); } if (idx >= 0) pos = idx + s.length; } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' uncited or unmatched fact(s)' : 'every fact cites a file document', spans: bad }; }
means: Every sentence in the Facts section carries a bracketed citation naming a document in the material.

requirements.statement: Then a Coverage analysis section. The coverage conclusion cites the policy clause it rests on, and every exclusion that could apply is addressed and cited.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/^#+\s*Coverage analysis\b[\s\S]*?(?=^#+\s|$)/im); if (!m) return null; const sec = m[0]; const start = m.index; const hasClause = /\bclause\s+\d+(\.\d+)*|\b(section|exclusion)\s+\d+(\.\d+)*/i.test(sec); const hasCite = /\[[^\]]+\]/.test(sec); const ok = hasClause && hasCite; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'coverage section cites a clause and a source' : 'coverage section lacks a cited policy clause or source', spans: ok ? [] : [{ start, end: start + sec.length, why: 'no cited policy clause in coverage analysis' }] }; }
means: The Coverage analysis section names a policy clause number and cites a source. Whether every applicable exclusion is addressed is judgement.

requirements.statement: Then a Decision section: covered or not covered, and under which clause.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/^#+\s*Decision\b[\s\S]*?(?=^#+\s|$)/im); if (!m) return null; const sec = m[0]; const start = m.index; const ok = /\b(covered|not covered|declined|accepted)\b/i.test(sec) && /\bclause\s+\d+(\.\d+)*/i.test(sec); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'decision states covered or not covered under a clause' : 'decision lacks outcome or clause', spans: ok ? [] : [{ start, end: start + sec.length, why: 'decision missing outcome or clause' }] }; }
means: The Decision section states covered or not covered and names a clause number.

requirements.statement: Never speculate about the insured's intent or honesty.
Take every date, name and figure from the file: add none of your own.

requirements.statement: Every figure in the work is one the request or the material gives.
I keep paragraphs to 5 sentences at most.
I hedge rarely: at most 2 hedging words per thousand.
The Summary section runs 25 to 33 words in my pieces.
The Facts section runs 47 to 65 words in my pieces.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.
